answer: One identity binds to one state-issued amateur radio callsign. The applicant passes a Morse exam, pays 600, and the regulator registers callsign, station and key: one callsign backs exactly one identity; two on one vertex collapse into one. No one can forge a callsign: the live check rejects it. Weight comes only after 120 days of logged operation, relayed by a repeater above the jetty. Per fake: 600 units plus 120 days; 100 fakes cost 60,000 units and 12,000 days. Cheapest cheat: buying a licensed callsign for 1,500 units, but the seller surrenders the callsign anchoring their own identity.
